items.risk: AI/cloud order growth can be constrained by optical-component supply and order-to-revenue timing.
Reported operating margin was negative due to accelerated restructuring, creating a meaningful comparable-versus-reported earnings distinction.
Capacity additions can arrive after demand normalizes, shifting a current shortage into utilization risk.
Restructuring creates real near-term cash costs even where comparable profitability improves.
Longer-term customer orders formed during component scarcity may expose Nokia to timing, mix or demand-normalization risk.
Manufacturing expansion intended to relieve optical bottlenecks increases execution and future utilization exposure.
Independent reporting still reflects company-reported quarter data; it corroborates the reported results and demand context but does not independently audit the underlying accounting records.
A raised annual outlook can still be missed if AI/cloud order conversion, component availability, or restructuring execution deteriorates later in 2026.

Underlying comparable profitability improved while reported profitability was negative because restructuring was accelerated.
contradictions.disposition: reconcilable accounting/economic distinction; preserve both views rather than treat as unresolved fraud or deterioration
